subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should skill-publish source flags be deprecated as non-visible client hints, stored and exposed as explicitly unverified attribution, or replaced by a server-verified GitHub publishing workflow?
rationale: Each option changes the public trust model, compatibility contract, and UI/API semantics; source inspection can confirm the current boundary but cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Clarify and deprecate hints
options.body: Keep trusted provenance server-resolved, document the existing flags as non-visible client hints, warn on their use for skill publishing, and plan removal if no internal consumer requires them.

options.title: Expose unverified attribution
options.body: Persist the client claim in a separately named and unmistakably unverified field that never influences verification, trust badges, or install decisions.

options.title: Build verified publishing
options.body: Authenticate and resolve the repository, commit, path, and uploaded content server-side before storing trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Clarify and deprecate hints
recommendation.body: Keep trusted provenance server-resolved, document the existing flags as non-visible client hints, warn on their use for skill publishing, and plan removal if no internal consumer requires them.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged GitHub-backed source work defines the adjacent trusted-provenance architecture and its verification behavior.
